title: Why You Keep Replaying Conversations in Your Head
header: Why you replay conversations at night
description:
It's 2am and you're still replaying something you said hours ago. Here's why your mind does it, and the one question that helps you let it go.

The Human Side: stories, insights and perspectives on the things we feel but rarely talk about.

scenes.text: It's two in the morning, and you're still replaying something you said at lunch.
scenes.query: woman awake in bed at night

scenes.text: Every word. Every pause. The look on their face.
So why does your mind keep doing this?
Because to your brain, a conversation is never just small talk. It's a quiet test of whether you still belong.
So it rewinds the moment again and again, searching for the part you might have gotten wrong.
Psychologists call this post-event processing. And here's what most people never realize.
The other person probably isn't replaying it at all.
Research on the spotlight effect shows we consistently overestimate how much others notice our mistakes.
So tonight, when the replay starts, ask yourself one question.
Would I judge a friend this harshly for the same moment?
You're allowed to let the conversation end.
